description: I’m a 16-year-old O Level student with no coding background, and this is my first hackathon. In one week I taught myself HTML, CSS and JavaScript, using AI as a tutor. I built Mission Architect, a game where players design a space mission, balance budget, weight, power and data, and learn why missions succeed or fail. My teammate, a computer science graduate, joined to help with testing. I joined to start my journey in software development.
summary: Mission Architect is a browser game that teaches how real space missions are designed. Players choose a destination (the Moon, Mars or Europa), a rocket, a power system, an antenna and science instruments, all within a limited budget. Every choice has a cost in money, weight, power or data, so there is no perfect design. When the player launches, the game simulates the mission and explains exactly why it succeeded or failed. It helps students see that space engineering is about trade-offs, not just building the biggest rocket.
details:
Mission Architect follows the four mission segments in NASA’s mission design overview: launch (the rocket), space (spacecraft, power and instruments), ground (the antenna that sends data home) and users (the science points players earn).

Players watch four live meters (budget, weight, power and data) and a spacecraft bay that shows each part they add. If a limit is exceeded, the meter turns red and Commander Zara, a guide character, explains the problem in simple words, for example what “payload capacity” or “data rate” means. Launching animates the rocket flying to the chosen planet, or crashing, followed by a full report of why.

Extra features: a welcome tutorial for beginners, three difficulty levels, random space weather (solar storms and radio interference) that is forecast in advance so players can plan, and a team mode for up to four players on one computer, where each player controls one role and must coordinate with the others.

Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript only. It runs in any browser with nothing to install.

the github project link to view code is : https://github.com/khizarashraf/mission-architect

AI (Claude, by Anthropic) was used as a tutor and coding assistant to help write and explain the HTML, CSS and JavaScript code and it helped to comment the code where it was needed.

This project uses NASA’s mission design resources from the challenge’s Resources page. The game’s structure follows the four mission segments (launch, space, ground, user) in NASA’s “Design and Develop Science Missions” overview. The game’s numbers are simplified and invented for learning, and are not real mission data.
